text:
maria: Heads-up — after the control plane separation peering cutover at 22:03 UTC we started seeing intermittent BGP route flaps from multiple tenant VPCs towards relay-az2 and relay-az3. Customer-facing private endpoints spiked 5xx.
jon: I'm on it. seeing a lot of `BGP/NOTIFICATION` and neighbor resets on rtr-relay-az2.
kevin: Which change specifically? the peering target swap or the new route-map we pushed?
maria: The repo change was the peering target switch (regional -> per-customer-edge) + small route-map to prefer local relays.
jon: Pulled BGP logs — snippets:
```
Mar 21 22:03:12 rtr-relay-az2 bgpd[2153]: neighbor 10.10.2.1 (AS 65021) state changed from Established to Idle
Mar 21 22:03:13 rtr-relay-az2 bgpd[2153]: received NOTIFICATION (neighbor 10.10.2.1): error code 3, subcode 1
```
aditya: Error code 3 = UPDATE error. Could be malformed attribute after we injected route-map. Did we touch AS_PATH or NEXT_HOP? 
kevin: Route-map only set `local-preference` and `community` but we also had a small eBGP export ACL tweak that might be truncating attributes.
laura: infra-bot: rollout `ctrl-plane-peering` completed at 22:03:07 UTC. No rollback initiated.
maria: Can someone run `show ip bgp neighbors 10.10.2.1 received-routes` on relay-az2 and relay-az3 and paste differences?
jon: Got it. relay-az2 shows many `Attribute length mismatch` entries. relay-az3 looks fine — so this is AZ-local.
kevin: That suggests the config we pushed to az2 included the ACL change but az3 didn't get it (partial rollout). Oops, partial config drift during canary.
aditya: If it's attribute truncation on send, the neighbor will drop the update -> flap. We should stop advertising the modified routes from az2 until we fix.
maria: Agreed. Can we flip az2 peering back to the legacy export policy and stop the new route-map? That should reduce flaps quickly.
kevin: I'll push a hotfix to undo the ACL on az2 only. Doing a targeted config push and will monitor.
jon: After the override — bgp neighbor stabilized. 22:12 UTC shows Established again.
laura: infra-bot: config-change hotfix `undo-acl-az2` applied at 22:11:40 UTC by kevin.
maria: Monitoring now — 5xxs trending down. We'll keep the hotfix for 2 hours and then plan a controlled, validated rollout.
aditya: For the RFC follow-up: we need stronger preflight for route attribute changes, and ensure our canary pushes include BGP attribute validation.
kevin: Also add a safety: if route-update errors exceed X/min, automatically revert the recent route-map/ACL on that AZ.
jon: Can we add a lightweight BGP sanity check in the deployment pipeline that runs `bgp parse` against the candidate policy? Might catch length/attr issues.
maria: Action items:
- kevin: keep hotfix on az2 for 2h, then coordinated rollback/patch (owner)
- aditya: draft RFC addendum for preflight checks + rollback triggers (owner)
- jon: add probing/monitoring alert for BGP update errors (owner)
- laura: log timeline + customer impact for postmortem (owner)

laura: I'll open a short incident doc and tag CS for customers who saw errors.
kevin: Patch plan: revert ACL change, then reintroduce route-map in staging with `bgp attribute` linting. ETA 24h.
aditya: For long-term: consider moving BGP attribute checks into our config-as-code linter and require a simulated `update-encode` step.
maria: Good. Let's also add a note in the control plane separation RFC about per-AZ config hygiene and canary rollbacks.
jon: +1
laura: I'll create the incident doc now and tag the followups. Thanks y'all. :thumbsup:
